narrator_001_woke_up: <speak>When I was nine, I woke up at four in the morning, and something was sitting on my bed.</speak>
narrator_002_not_the_end: <speak>Not at the end of it, where a dog would sleep. It was halfway up the blanket, crouched over my knees.</speak>
narrator_003_thin_man: <speak>It was shaped like a man. A very thin man. No hair. No clothes. Skin the color of candle wax.</speak>
narrator_004_claws: <speak>Its hands were spread on the blanket, and the fingers were far too long. Each one ended in a curved yellow claw, like the teeth of a rake.</speak>
narrator_006_watched: <speak>It didn't blink. It didn't breathe. It just watched.</speak>
narrator_007_counted: <speak>I pulled the covers over my face and counted to ten.</speak>
narrator_008_gone: <speak>When I looked again, it was gone.</speak>
narrator_009_moved: <speak>That summer, we had moved into my grandmother's old house. She'd died in the spring, and my dad couldn't bear to sell it.</speak>
narrator_010_his_room: <speak>I got the little bedroom at the end of the hall. The room that used to be his.</speak>
lily_001_man_on_bed: <speak>Dad, there was a man on my bed last night. A skinny man with really long fingers.</speak>
dad_001_nightmare: <speak>That's a nightmare, bug. New house, new noises. Everybody gets them.</speak>
lily_002_four: <speak>It was four o'clock. I looked at the clock.</speak>
narrator_013_smiled: <speak>Just for a second. Then he smiled, kissed the top of my head, and told me to stop reading scary books before bed.</speak>
narrator_015_attic: <speak>That weekend, Dad sent me up to the attic to find the box fan.</speak>
narrator_016_notebook: <speak>Behind the boxes there was a little blue notebook with a broken lock. My grandmother's handwriting. Nineteen eighty-four.</speak>
narrator_017_changed: <speak>Most of it was boring. Church. Groceries. The weather. And then, near the end, the handwriting changed.</speak>
grandma_001_june: <speak>June eleventh. Something came into the house last night.</speak>
grandma_002_danny: <speak>It sat on Danny's bed and watched him sleep.</speak>
grandma_003_mother: <speak>My mother told me about it when I was a girl. I thought it was a story to keep children in bed.</speak>
grandma_004_rule: <speak>The first time, it only watches. The second time, it comes closer. The third time<break time="420ms"/> it says your name.</speak>
grandma_005_our_room: <speak>Danny sleeps in our room now. I will not let it come back.</speak>
narrator_018_last_page: <speak>That was the last page. The rest had been torn out.</speak>
narrator_019_daniel: <speak>My dad's name is Daniel. When he was a boy, everyone called him Danny.</speak>
narrator_020_mine_now: <speak>And his room, the little bedroom at the end of the hall, was mine now.</speak>
narrator_021_showed: <speak>I showed him the diary. I watched him read it twice.</speak>
lily_003_closer: <speak>Dad, it said the second time it comes closer. It was on my bed. It was right on top of me.</speak>
narrator_022_not_a_dream: <speak>He didn't say "it was a dream" this time.</speak>
narrator_023_sleep_with_mom: <speak>He said I was sleeping with Mom tonight. And he would sleep in my room.</speak>
narrator_024_couldnt: <speak>I tried to stay awake. I couldn't.</speak>
narrator_025_four: <speak>I woke up at four in the morning.</speak>
narrator_026_silent: <speak>The house was completely silent. No clock. No wind. Nothing.</speak>
narrator_027_voice: <speak>And then, through the wall, very softly, I heard a voice I had never heard before. Thin and dry, like paper tearing.</speak>
narrator_028_mom: <speak>Mom didn't wake up. I still don't know how she didn't wake up.</speak>
narrator_029_ran: <speak>I ran down the hall. My bedroom door was open. The lamp was on.</speak>
narrator_031_torn: <speak>The blanket had been torn open in three long lines, from the pillow to the end of the bed. Like something had raked it.</speak>
narrator_038_wallet: <speak>A week later, Mom gave me his wallet. Folded inside it, very small, were the pages missing from Grandma's diary.</speak>
grandma_006_june14: <speak>June fourteenth. Robert slept in Danny's bed last night, so it would find him instead.</speak>
grandma_007_name: <speak>At four o'clock, I heard it say his name. My husband is gone.</speak>
grandma_008_rule: <speak>Mother was right. It never takes the child. It takes whoever lies down in the child's place.</speak>
narrator_039_knew: <speak>My dad tore those pages out himself, when he was nine. He knew exactly what was coming.</speak>
narrator_040_anyway: <speak>And he lay down in my bed anyway.</speak>
narrator_041_moved: <speak>Mom and I moved eight hundred miles away. I never went back to that house.</speak>
narrator_042_grew_up: <speak>I grew up. I had a son. For twenty-five years, I told myself it was the house.</speak>
narrator_043_sam: <speak>Sam is nine now. This morning, at breakfast, he asked me a question.</speak>
son_002_watches: <speak>The one who sits at the end of my bed. He doesn't do anything. He just watches.</speak>
son_003_closer: <speak>Mom<break time="420ms"/> he came closer last night. He put his hand on my knee.</speak>
narrator_047_lay_down: <speak>I put Sam in my bed. Then I walked down the hall, and lay down in his.</speak>
narrator_049_climbed: <speak>Something climbed up from the end of the bed. Slowly. Knees. Hands. Closer.</speak>
narrator_050_looked: <speak>This time, I didn't hide. I looked right at it.</speak>
narrator_051_glad: <speak>Sam. If you're reading this, it took me instead of you. I'm glad.</speak>
narrator_052_never_wanted: <speak>It never wanted children. It visits them three times<break time="420ms"/> and waits to see who loves them enough to lie down in their place.</speak>
narrator_053_someone: <speak>My grandfather did it for my dad. My dad did it for me. Someone always does. Maybe that is what keeps it alive.</speak>
narrator_054_starve: <speak>Maybe if, just once, nobody lay down<break time="420ms"/> it would finally starve.</speak>
narrator_055_couldnt: <speak>I couldn't find out. Not with you.</speak>
narrator_056_decide: <speak>One day, your own child will ask you about the skinny man. And you'll have to decide.</speak>
